list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.12
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.12
**Release channel:** `beta`

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The equalizer can make a profile of its own, not only import one.** The list held *No equalization*, every AutoEQ `ParametricEQ.txt` imported on the machine and the bundled example, so a profile that did not come from a file did not exist: shaping one's own curve meant importing a file with no filters in it first. A **New profile** row sits between the profiles and the import now, and it asks for a name before it makes the profile (`new_profile`, all 49 languages): the profile joins the list with the ten bands the chart already draws, every gain at 0 dB and the app's own Q, becomes the active one and opens the editor on a flat line, so the first thing to move is the curve the listener can see. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` passes; `:desktop:equalizerRenderCheck` reads `no profile: cards=1 rows=5` and `profile: cards=4 rows=17` (the five list rows, the curve, the preamp and the ten bands), with the curve still painted in `37660 px` and the fold still opening and closing. In the preview the row opens the same one-field dialog, and a created profile reads `No equalization`, the three shipped profiles, `My headphones`, `New profile`, `Import profile (.txt)`, `Add example profile`, with `My headphones` selected and its ten bands at `0 dB`; `styles_check.mjs`, `scroll_check.mjs`, `motion_check.mjs`, `prefs_check.mjs`, `buttons_check.mjs`, `geometry_check.mjs` and `glyph_check.mjs` exit 0. **Watch:** a profile can start empty of gains but never empty of bands, and it is the active profile as soon as it exists. **Open sub-item:** the created profile's name is asked once and cannot be renamed from the equalizer afterwards, and nothing here presses the dialog in the app itself, which has no pointer in a headless read.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.12: make an equalizer profile by hand

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.11
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.11
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The Apple player's five controls are one group in the middle of the column, on the artwork's own axis.** 1.56.9 spread them with `SpaceEvenly` over the column's whole width, so the shuffle and the repeat sat against its edges and the row read wider than the cover above it: two rows on the column's outer edges instead of one group under the picture. They are gathered at the expressive player's own distance (`Arrangement.spacedBy(20.dp, Alignment.CenterHorizontally)`) now, so the group is centred on the artwork's axis at every width and the play glyph stays the row's centre, and the phone's glyph sizes (48 dp skips, 80 dp play, 20 dp shuffle and repeat) are untouched. Nothing else on that screen moved. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` passes; `:desktop:applePlayerRenderCheck` reads the same `7141 ink px in the column` (the same five glyphs, in a new place), the window's four corners still at 59 / 67 / 12 / 12 and `0 ink px right of the column` at 640x800. The preview mirrors it: `justify-content: center` with a 20 px gap, and `styles_check.mjs`, `scroll_check.mjs` and `motion_check.mjs` exit 0. **Watch:** the group is centred, nothing in it is spread; a width is not what separates the five. **Open sub-item:** the screen keeps the reference's two columns, the cover and the controls in the left one, so "centred" here means on the artwork's axis and not in the middle of the window; a single centred column with the lyrics underneath would be a different screen.
- [DE] **The rotating artwork is a squared cover, in the player and in the three mini players, and the cookie is what it draws when the rotation is off.** The picture used to keep the 4-sided cookie while it turned, so its corners swung around a fixed outline, and the mini players each carried a fixed corner of their own whatever the option said. The shape now comes from one place, `trackArtworkShape(rotating)`: a level of the theme's shape scale while the artwork revolves (`MaterialTheme.shapes.medium`) and `CookieShapes.fourSided` at rest, read by the player's big artwork and by the classic, new and Apple mini player's thumbnail alike, so the four cannot disagree about one switch. The wrappers that hold an artwork follow it: the two players' shadows, the expressive player's title scrim and the Apple player's elevation are the same shape as the picture they sit under. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` passes and `:desktop:applePlayerRenderCheck` exits 0. The preview mirrors it (`artworkShapeClass` in js/player.js, `.cover.cover--squared` in css/app.css) and its three checks exit 0. **Watch:** an artwork's shape is `trackArtworkShape(rotating)`, never a fixed `CookieShapes` value, when the surface can rotate; the option decides the shape family, not only the movement. **Open sub-item:** the option is off by default, so the screenshots of the mini players in this release still read as the cookie; nothing here renders the spinning state headlessly, so the squared shape is verified as the shape it hands over, not as a frame of the rotation.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.11-beta: the Apple player's group and the rotating shape

---

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.10
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.10
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The app stops re-running its whole UI every two seconds, and the dev stats stop launching PowerShell every two seconds.** Two drains on the same path, both visible in the exported session of 28 Oct 21:36. The window title was built in the composable body that hosts the entire app, out of `SystemMonitor.stats`, which ticks every 2 s: each tick re-executed that body, and with it the sidebar, the open screen and the player, because a parameter list with a `List` in it is not skippable. That is measurable: `app.log` held 248 copies of each of the four `startup:` lines in twelve minutes, and `playlists.log` 167 copies of the same sidebar line. The live part of the title is written on the AWT frame from a coroutine now, one collector over its four inputs plus a 400 ms re-assert so a title Compose writes back from the `title` parameter is corrected instead of staying on screen, and the composition only ever sees the constant base title. The four startup stages also stop reading the settings store to decide that they have nothing to write (once per process), and the sidebar's account-playlist filter is `remember`ed with its log line in a `LaunchedEffect` instead of on every pass. The second drain: `windowsNetTotals` launched `powershell.exe` on every sample, i.e. a whole process every two seconds for as long as developer options were on. The counters are read from `netstat -e` by POSITION now (its labels are localized, its numbers are not, and the first row that carries two numbers is always received then sent) on their own 10 s cadence (`NET_SAMPLE_MS`), with the PowerShell pipeline kept as the fallback for an output that does not parse, and the sampler runs on the IO dispatcher because a sample can launch a process. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` passes; on this machine `netstat -e` takes 88 ms and prints `Byte 1349517760 566390993`, which the new parse reads, while the PowerShell pipeline it replaces takes 2085 ms. **Watch:** a value that changes on a timer is read by a coroutine that writes it into AWT or into a child composable, never in the body that hosts the app, and the OS network counters are sampled on `NET_SAMPLE_MS`. **Open sub-item:** nothing here measures the frame time of the running app, so the win is the removal of the two causes the log proves, not a before/after frame time.
- [DE] **A lyrics provider that answers with a web page is reported as that instead of as a JSON dump.** The session log showed `Musixmatch: Illegal input: Unexpected JSON token at offset 0: Expected start of the object '{', but had '<' instead at path: $` followed by the page's own `<html>` line, which says nothing about what happened and puts markup in a support export. A failure that carries that markup is now logged as `answered with an HTML page instead of JSON (blocked or rate limited)`, whatever the provider. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` passes. **Open sub-item:** the blocked answer is still not retried on another route, it is only named correctly.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.10-beta: stop the two-second UI re-run
- docs: record the preview's player backgrounds in the todo

---
This release was built automatically from commit `c89c60ddc53eea159cc19b064660c3e8ee2a9b26`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.9
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.9
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The Apple player's transport is the phone's Apple player, size for size.** The row was drawn at a second and smaller scale than `Player_v2.kt` uses on the phone: 30 dp skip glyphs and a 42 dp play glyph, gathered in the middle of the column with a gap that followed its width, so the play button was half the size of the reference's and the five controls read as a strip of equal icons. It is the phone's row now - skip previous and next at 48 dp, play/pause at 80 dp, the shuffle and the repeat small (20 dp on a 40 dp target, so the picture stays small and the hit area does not) - spread over the column with `Arrangement.SpaceEvenly`, which is what the phone uses. Nothing else on the row changed: the glyphs still lift on hover, the tooltips are the same, and the row keeps its place between the times and the volume. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` passes; `:desktop:applePlayerRenderCheck` reads `1280x800: mean brightness 0,06, 7141 ink px in the column, 8857 in the lyrics` (5872 before the change, the row being the difference) and the four corners of the window still at 59 / 67 / 12 / 12; in the preview `styles_check.mjs`, `scroll_check.mjs` and `motion_check.mjs` exit 0. **Watch:** the transport's glyph sizes are the phone's 48 / 80, not a scale of the column - a column wide or narrow keeps the same buttons, and the row spreads the space between them. **Open sub-item:** nothing presses the new glyphs headlessly, so the sizes are verified as pixels and as computed sizes in the preview, not by clicking them.
- [DE] **The preview's Apple player is the same row, and one column under 720 px.** The five controls carry the same 20 / 48 / 80 sizes in the same targets (`flex: 0 0 auto`, so the flexbox cannot shrink the play button below its 88 px), spread with `space-evenly`; and below 720 px the screen draws one centred column and no lyrics, the rule `AppleMusicPlayer` already applies, where the preview had kept 34 % of the width for the column and left a 163 px strip with half a window empty beside it. **Measured:** `styles_check.mjs` reads 17 sheets with every corner a scale level and every colour a role, `scroll_check.mjs` reads 51 screens at 1440x900 and 820x800 with no scrollbar and every cut text on hover, `motion_check.mjs` exits 0; the row computes `space-evenly`, `gap: 0`, and 36 / 64 / 88 / 64 / 36 px targets around 20 / 48 / 80 px glyphs. Only gitignored preview files changed on that half, so no separate version was bumped for it.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.9-beta: the Apple player's transport at the phone's sizes

---

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.8
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.8
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The Apple Music player's backdrop covers the window, and the screen follows the background chosen in the settings.** Two defects on one screen. `BlurredBackdrop` applied its fill scale *inside* `Modifier.blur`, whose layer is the node's own 256 dp and clips what it blurs, so the "Apple Music" and "Blur" styles painted one 256 dp square in the middle of the window and left everything around it black. And `AppleMusicPlayer` drew a second backdrop of its own, fixed to `PlayerBackgroundStyle.APPLE_MUSIC`, over the one `PlayerScreen` already paints behind every design, so a background picked in *Player & mini-player design* never showed here. The scale now sits outside the blur layer (still one 256 dp raster, scaled to the window), the player draws no backdrop of its own so the screen's own - which already follows the setting - is the only one, and the `accent` and `background` parameters that only fed it are gone with it. That also removes the two canvases (or two blurs) that would otherwise animate with one of them hidden. The artwork is untouched: still the 4-sided cookie, still with its shadow.

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The Apple Music player's transport is one group in the middle of the column, and play is a glyph instead of a disc.** The five controls were spread with `SpaceBetween`, so the distance between two of them was whatever the column happened to be wide: a narrow window nearly touched the icons, and a wide one left the play button alone in a row of empty space. They are `spacedBy(gap, CenterHorizontally)` now, with the gap following the column between 4 and 24 dp so the group never grows into the row's edges and never overflows a narrow one. Play/pause is the biggest glyph of that row rather than a 52 dp white circle, the way the reference draws it, and it is wrapped in a `Tooltip` like the other four.
- [DE] **`applePlayerRenderCheck` paints a track with a cover now, so the backdrop is measured.** Its fixture had no artwork on purpose, which is the case the scrim exists for and also the only case in which the broken backdrop was invisible: the check passed while the real screen painted one small square. It renders both, generates a flat green cover into `.ignore/appleplayer/artwork.png` instead of depending on an asset, and fails when a corner of the window is not the artwork's colour. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` passes; `:desktop:applePlayerRenderCheck` reads `1280x800: mean brightness 0,06, 5872 ink px in the column, 8857 in the lyrics` and `with artwork: top-left 59, top-right 67, bottom-left 12, bottom-right 12`, `640x800: 0 ink px right of the column`; putting the scale back inside the blur makes the same case fail with all four corners at `-3 / -3 / 0 / 0` naming `the blurred backdrop does not reach the... corner of the window` (the mutation was reverted). `:desktop:playerDesignRenderCheck` exits 0, and in the preview `styles_check.mjs`, `scroll_check.mjs` and `motion_check.mjs` exit 0 with the Apple screen drawn at 1280x800 and 640x800. **Watch:** a backdrop that has to cover its box scales the blurred layer, never a layer inside it; a full-player design does not paint `PlayerBackground` itself, because the screen already does with the style the user chose. **Open sub-item:** the check has no pointer and no display, so the transport group and the play glyph are verified as pixels in the two PNGs and in the preview, not by pressing them.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.8-beta: the Apple player's backdrop and transport

---
